First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡y\cdot (-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{yxx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yxx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{yx}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡y\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
